name: STAR Orbit — two-body propagation (universal variables)
summary: Kepler propagation with universal variables and Stumpff functions: no orbit-geometry singularity (circular, equatorial, elliptic, hyperbolic), whole periods removed, bracketed root with bounded iterations, explicit refusals.
reference: Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, Example 2-4 (Kepler's problem): r = (-4219.7527, 4363.0292, -3958.7666) km, v = (3.689866, -1.916735, -6.112511) km/s after 40 min
reference_observed: position error 4.7e-5 km and velocity error 2.5e-7 km/s against the printed values; 450 closed-form orbits to 4.7e-7 km

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: any consistent units; default mu in km^3/s^2
review.G-06: no external data; corpus generated from closed-form equations in the tests
review.G-08: pure function, standard library only, no IO
review.G-13: ValueError for invalid input before any iteration, RuntimeError when the iteration budget is exhausted, bounded loops
